summary: Palatine immigrant of 1739 from Ulmet who farmed in Plainfield Township, Pennsylvania; John's 7th-great-grandfather if the Doll line holds, and not a Revolutionary captain.
bio:
Johann Casper Doll was baptized on 1 February 1722 in the Lutheran parish of Ulmet in the Kusel district of the Palatinate, a son of Christoffel Doll (1671-1739) and Anna Sara Schuch; the family came from the village of Erzweiler. His godparents included a Schuch, from his mother's family, and the wife of Christian Drum of Ulmet. His gravestone gives his birth as 2 February 1724, but the parish register is the better authority.

In 1739, aged eighteen, he sailed for Pennsylvania on the ship Samuel, qualifying at Philadelphia on 27 August and signing the list with a mark. With him were Stoffel Doll, 40, Philip Doll, 27, 'Christ. Shook', 48, of his mother's Schuch family, and Simon Drum, a party from Ulmet. He married Anna Margaretha Dietz, and their daughter Anna Catharine was baptized in 1757 at Tohickon Reformed Church in Bucks County. He farmed in Plainfield Township, Northampton County, where he died on 4 February 1793, and was buried at Plainfield Cemetery near Wind Gap.

Family tradition has made him a captain in the Revolution, but he is not known to have held that rank; he was about 52 in 1776. The monument on his grave, erected in 1934, honours his nephew Capt. Casper Dull (1748-1829), who did serve as a captain and is buried at McVeytown, Mifflin County, and some records have run the two men together. If the Doll connection holds, Johann Casper Doll was John's 7th-great-grandfather.

researchNotes:
Johann Casper Doll was baptized 1 Feb 1722 at Ulmet, Kusel district, son of Christoffel Doll (1671-1739) and Anna Sara Schuch (WikiTree Doll-527, FamilySearch N5BL-88G); his gravestone gives 2 Feb 1724 and the tree 1724-1793. WikiTree's API in Oct 2026 gave his birthplace as 'Oberland, Canton, Switzerland' (unsupported; Ulmet treated as probable). Round 3 corrected his arrival: 'Casper Doll, age 18' was on the ship Samuel (Hugh Percy), qualified at Philadelphia 27 Aug 1739 (Strassburger List 69 A; signature 'Caspar (X) Doll'), with Stoffel Doll 40, Philip Doll 27, 'Christ. Shook, 48' (Schuch) and Simon Drum - a group from Ulmet; the Samuel of 30 Aug 1737 (List 44), cited earlier, has no Casper. He married Anna Margaretha Dietz; a daughter Anna Catharine was baptized in 1757 at Tohickon Reformed Church, Bucks Co., to 'Casper Doll and Margaret [Dietz]'. He died 4 Feb 1793 and is buried at Plainfield Cemetery, Plainfield Twp (Wind Gap), Northampton Co. (Find a Grave 19353732). The tree calls him 'Johann C Doll Captain' with a 'FLAG OF THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION' profile image, but 'he is NOT known to have held the rank as captain. On his gravesite, there was erected in 1934 a monument or cenotaph to his nephew Casper Dull who served as a captain in the Revolutionary War'; that nephew, Capt. Casper Dull (1748-1829), is buried at McVeytown, Mifflin Co. His Find a Grave memorial merges the two. He was about 52 in 1776. No SAR patriot record for him was found (search not exhaustive); DAR unchecked.

Round 4 read the image of the Ulmet Lutheran baptism register (1722, p.245) that FamilySearch attaches to his profile. Johann Caspar, child of Christoffel Doll and Anna Sara, was baptized on 1 Feb 1722 ([R4-S1]). One godparent appears to be a Schuch, which fits his mother's maiden name, Schuch. Another is the wife of Christian Drum of Ulmet, and a Simon Drum sailed with the Dolls on the Samuel in 1739. The register therefore confirms the Ulmet baptism and his parents' names, and it outweighs the 2 Feb 1724 date on his gravestone. FamilySearch (M7ZN-ZBL) labels him 'Capt.' and attaches a Historical Society of Pennsylvania burial card for 'Capt Casper Doll or Dull'; that card belongs to the nephew, Capt. Casper Dull (1748-1829), as the existing bio already explains. The burial-card image downloaded as 0 bytes. The village in the 1722 entry is Erzweiler: the 1704 Ulmet marriage of his parents calls his father 'Hans Peter Dollen Sohn zu Erzweiler' (see H0080).
